emma_cs: FYI customer ACME (acct: acct-0a1b2c) says their month-end invoice total ($12,451.20) doesn't match dashboard ($8,603.47). They flagged extra line items and plan tier on invoice shows 'Pro' but customer is on 'Enterprise'. Can someone triage?
omar_billing: Invoice ID and PDF? Also need month range.
emma_cs: Invoice 2026-03-31-INV-00421, period 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-31. Customer pasted CSV of line items — I'll drop a sanitized sample below.
emma_cs: ```
line_item,description,units,unit_price,amount
embedding_requests,embedding units,2,0.00075,0.0015
text_generation,tokens,12000000,0.0008,9600.00
chat_tokens,tokens,3500000,0.0008,2800.00
plan_fee,monthly enterprise plan,1,950.00,950.00
overage_marker,unknown,1,100.70,100.70
```
emma_cs: Dashboard shows total tokens 11,000,000 and plan fee $0 (customer has enterprise commit). So two discrepancies: token counts and plan fee.
omar_billing: Hmm, that stray overage_marker looks suspect. Can you confirm billing product codes in invoice vs internal mapping? Passing to billing pipeline owners.
kai_infra: tagging this for infra — any chance usage ingestion lagged for final day? We had TTL backfill job on 2026-03-31 23:52 that processed a late batch. If the invoice generation window closed before backfill, that could explain invoice > dashboard (invoice picked up post-cutoff, dashboard shows current).
emma_cs: Customer insists invoice is higher than dashboard, so invoice must include extra tokens not visible in UI. They want credit if billing is wrong.
billing-bot: Automated notice: invoice 2026-03-31-INV-00421 generated at 2026-04-01T02:03:15Z. Billing run window: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z - 2026-03-31T23:59:59Z. Raw usage export available at /exports/acct-0a1b2c/2026-03-usage.csv
omar_billing: Can someone run a quick diff between raw export and dashboard-aggregated numbers? Prefer SQL.
kai_infra: Running a quick query against usage_events table for acct-0a1b2c last 48h of March: 
```sql
SELECT event_type, sum(tokens) as tokens, min(received_at) as first_seen
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct-0a1b2c' AND received_at >= '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY event_type;
```
kai_infra: Early result shows ~3.6M chat tokens received after 2026-03-31T23:55:00Z due to a retry storm from one client job. Those were ingested but flagged with source=legacy-ingest. Dashboard aggregation pipeline filters out source=legacy-ingest until mapping is validated. Invoice includes all ingested tokens (raw), dashboard excludes them — that would explain invoice > dashboard.
omar_billing: That explains token delta. What about plan fee showing as $0 on dashboard?
pat_sre: I see a webhook mislabeling in account metadata sync on 2026-03-30 04:12Z — account tier got temporarily set to 'pro' in billing_metadata table because the sync job failed and retried with fallback mapping. Invoices read billing_metadata snapshot at invoice time. Dashboard reads current tier from customer profile service (which was corrected on 2026-03-30 05:01Z). So invoice captured a stale/provisional tier.
emma_cs: So two separate causes: late ingestion from legacy source plus metadata sync fallback. Customer wants a clear explanation and a goodwill credit for the plan fee and possibly token overage.
omar_billing: Proposed remediation: 1) Issue billing adjustment reversing the erroneous plan fee line (INV-CREDIT-00421) 2) For token overage, compute overlap: mark tokens with source=legacy-ingest and received_at >= invoice_cutoff and exclude if dashboard excludes them — propose credit for those tokens. Need approval from finance.
ai_note: (not a message, internal) — ensure adjustments are idempotent and include audit trail.
pat_sre: I'll open INC-2026-45 and assign to billing+finance. Also adding a panic flag for invoice generator so we don't reference fallback metadata in future runs.
kai_infra: Quick mitigation: update dashboard aggregation to include source=legacy-ingest for 48-hour backfill window OR mark those tokens visible in the UI as 'delayed ingestion' so customers can see them.
emma_cs: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate after credits. Here are steps we used internally: 1) Download raw export: /exports/acct-0a1b2c/2026-03-usage.csv 2) Run the SQL to sum tokens by source and time window (example below) 3) Compare dashboard-aggregated numbers from the UI CSV export.
emma_cs: ```sql
-- tokens counted in invoice window but filtered from dashboard
SELECT source, sum(tokens) as tokens, count(*) as events
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id='acct-0a1b2c' AND received_at >= '2026-03-01' AND received_at < '2026-04-01'
  AND received_at >= '2026-03-31T23:55:00Z'
GROUP BY source;
```
omar_billing: I'll prepare a credit memo draft and send to finance for approval. ETA 24 hours.
pat_sre: created INC-2026-45, linked invoices INV-00421 and INV-CREDIT-00421 (pending). Assigning Omar and Kai.
emma_cs: Customer wants a short note to communicate: one-paragraph explanation + timeline + expected credit amount once finance approves. I'll draft once Omar gives numbers.
omar_billing: Draft numbers: errant plan fee 950.00 and legacy-ingest tokens ~3,600,000 tokens @ $0.0008 => 2,880.00 credit. Total provisional credit = 3,830.00. finance approval required.
pat_sre: tagging @finance and adding audit logs. Also recommends preventing fallback mapping in next billing run.
emma_cs: Thanks all — I'll update customer with provisional credit and INC ref. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Invoice adjustment IN-2026-CREDIT queued. Will post update when finance approves.
omar_billing: Follow-up: once finance signs off, we'll issue credit and regenerate corrected invoice PDF. I will paste the new invoice link here.
emma_cs: Customer replied: appreciate quick triage, asked for timeline. I gave them 48 hours.
pat_sre: Closing loop: please add any postmortem notes to #postmortems when incident resolved.
